failure_modes: Assay sensitivity floor: BODIPY C11, TBARS, and LC-MS cannot be adapted to the low total lipid/protein mass present in capture-positive eluates; signal-to-noise remains too low even after method optimization, producing non-reproducible readouts across lots (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Formulation/interferent confounding: residual surfactant, capture buffer components, or spike-in tracers chemically alter BODIPY or TBARS signals or quench fluorescence, producing artifactual oxidation/permeability readouts despite capture-compatibility controls (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Non-causal correlation: measured increases in oxidation/permeability do not precede or predict loss of immuno-capture co-localization or detergent/protease sensitivity — e.g., epitope masking, selective depletion of minor EV subpopulations, or reversible surface conformational changes account for capture loss without bulk membrane chemical damage (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Spike-in tracer failure-mode: spike-in recovery does not adequately control for capture-compatibility across exposure conditions (different binding kinetics or differential loss under shear/freezethaw), producing misleading per-sample assay validation and masking true assay failure (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Cross-species and delivery confound: even if chemical damage is real and associated with analytical signature loss in vitro, in vivo detectability and potency in larger animals or humans may be dominated by administration route, mucosal retention, or clearance (e.g., strong nasal retention and negligible brain uptake in macaque intranasal studies), making the gate irrelevant to translational outcome (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Overfitting to a process envelope: the defined freeze-thaw + surfactant + device-shear matrix may identify a specific, narrow prohibited envelope that is not the major cause of identity or potency loss observed in other failure modes (e.g., TFF stress, source-cell heterogeneity), so gating on this envelope would not prevent bridging failures (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

False reassurance from preserved particle counts: similar NTA/TRPS particle counts despite chemistry changes could lead to overreliance on count-based release metrics while the chemistry assay variability undermines interpretability, creating mixed messages for release decisions (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Translatability disconnect: preclinical intranasal efficacy in rodent models (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) suggests functional delivery can occur despite varied processing histories; thus a chemical gate that predicts in vitro signature loss may not map to loss of in vivo efficacy across species or indications, confounding its operational value (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus).
strongest_objection: The strongest bounded objection is that the proposed chemical-readout gate (BODIPY C11/TBARS/ox-PL LC-MS + permeability dye on capture-positive eluates) may either (A) lack the analytical sensitivity and specificity to detect meaningful membrane-chemical damage in low-biomass, capture-recovered EV fractions after exposure, or (B) detect chemistry changes that are epiphenomenal (correlated but not causal) with respect to loss of the intact-EV capture-protection signature or in vivo functional/identity loss. Either outcome would render the gate unmeasurable or misleading for process control: false negatives (missed damage because assays are below detection limits or interfered) would fail to protect downstream bridging decisions, while false positives (chemical signal that does not predict capture/protection loss or potency in relevant in vivo contexts) would incorrectly discard usable lots.
